data.why: The repo ships a built-in synthetic sample FITS used by the demo button; the same file is handed to the browser as an upload option to exercise the 'Upload my own FITS image' path.

goals: Load a raw FITS telescope image and see what faint structure is hidden in the pixel data
Compare linear, logarithmic, and asinh stretching to decide which best reveals faint detail without exaggerating noise
Adjust black/white point percentiles to avoid letting a few extreme pixels dominate the display range
Tune stretch strength to balance revealing faint structure against over-brightening the background
Inspect image dimensions, pixel statistics, and FITS header metadata (object, filter, exposure, observation date)
Review the pixel-value histogram to understand where black/white points fall relative to the data, then export the stretched result as a PNG

review.summary: The tree matches the README's stated purpose and workflow closely: load a FITS image, inspect its stats and header, compare stretch methods while tuning percentile clipping and strength against the histogram, then export a PNG for display. The evidence holds up, and the needed fixes are small: one wrong description of the histogram axis, an oversized source/summary feature that should be split, and some cleanup actions inside t2.
